question: Do you check the real price, or just the discount?
note: Daily news Short 2026-11-23 (Thanksgiving / Black Friday week). Confirmed: NRF press release Nov 19 2026 (Prosper survey of 7,956 adults, Oct 30-Nov 9): 182.7M expected to shop Thanksgiving weekend vs 186.9M last year (~-2%); 48% say deals 'too good to pass up'; matched by Chain Store Age and Mass Market Retailers (Nov 19). Adobe Digital Insights forecast Sep 28 2026: Cyber Week peak discounts up to 30% off list, 'on par with the 2025 season'; Black Friday online ~$12.9B forecast. Gus's $900->$499 TV is a made-up example, not a real deal. Nothing alleged. Psychology: anchoring, Tversky & Kahneman 1974, Science 185 (wheel rigged to 10 or 65; median estimates of % African countries in UN 25 vs 45).

post.title: Black Friday's "Was $900" Price Is a Trick on Your Brain #shorts
post.description: About 183 million people are expected to shop over Thanksgiving weekend, slightly fewer than last year, and 48% say the deals are "too good to pass up" (NRF survey, Nov 19). Adobe expects peak online discounts of up to about 30% this season, on par with 2025. Gus and Nell talk about anchoring: in Tversky & Kahneman's 1974 study, a random wheel landing on 10 or 65 pulled people's guesses to about 25% or 45%. That "was" price works the same way. Do you check the real price, or just the discount? Comment below. Sources: National Retail Federation (Nov 19, 2026); Chain Store Age (Nov 2026); Adobe Digital Insights holiday forecast (Sep 28, 2026); Tversky & Kahneman, Science (1974).
